searchText: Made a short post with some Sepolia and Mainnet data about the execution payload / block sizes we observed in the networks. Post also contains simulation results for different payload sizes propagations. Conclusion is with 8411 we are safe under the most strict assumptions (3 seconds for payload broadcast, eip 7870 limitations, increasing gas limits etc). https://notes.ethereum.org/@QiVhN6C0QRW_MyxL5s89MQ/ryuczVRizg cc <@&595681771690000403> <@&595681804422479873> <@439032863904628745> why did you simulate and not just test it on sepolia? We need a fork to enable 8411 on sepolia oh right Happy to test it on sepolia if clients support it. But this is the EIP for hegota, not glamsterdam Is this EIP not an optional one? Not optional. We need changes in the bid structure sorry I thought this was purely an (optional) networking eip Here is my digging into mainnet data for evidence from the past. Big block did cause some trouble when we had them. (big shout out to the Panda tool and its authors!) https://notes.ethereum.org/@cskiraly/large-block-reorg we should move the `ATTESTATION_DUE_BPS_GLOAS` to 2 seconds into the slot, there is 0 reason to have it at 3 seconds, this extra time is just eaten up by timing games anyways

excerpts.author: .just_kk
excerpts.content:
Made a short post with some Sepolia and Mainnet data about the execution payload / block sizes we observed in the networks.

Post also contains simulation results for different payload sizes propagations.

Conclusion is with 8411 we are safe under the most strict assumptions (3 seconds for payload broadcast, eip 7870 limitations, increasing gas limits etc).

https://notes.ethereum.org/@QiVhN6C0QRW_MyxL5s89MQ/ryuczVRizg
